quests.instruction: After twenty minutes on a screen, you look out the window at something far away for twenty seconds. Which parts are you giving a rest?
quests.hint: They work hard when you stare at something close.
quests.explanation: Looking far away relaxes the tiny muscles inside your eyes that focus on close things.
quests.funFact: People blink less when they stare at screens, which can make eyes feel dry.

quests.instruction: A cotton swab pushed deep into your ear could hurt which thin, drum-like skin?
quests.hint: It stretches across the inside of your ear.
quests.explanation: The eardrum sits at the end of the ear canal and is delicate, so nothing small should go deep into your ear.
quests.funFact: Your ears clean themselves, because wax slowly moves outward and carries dirt with it.

quests.instruction: If you get a nosebleed, you sit down, lean slightly forward, and pinch the soft part of which body part for about ten minutes?
quests.hint: Pinch below the hard, bony top, where it is soft.
quests.explanation: Pinching the soft part of the nose presses on tiny blood vessels so they can seal. Leaning forward keeps blood out of your throat.
quests.funFact: Nosebleeds are common in children, because the blood vessels inside the nose are close to the surface.

quests.instruction: When you sit in a chair, which part of your body should be supported by the chair's back?
quests.hint: It runs along the rear of your body.
quests.explanation: A chair back supports your spine, so your muscles do not have to work as hard.
quests.funFact: Changing position every so often is better than holding one perfect position for hours.

quests.instruction: When you type on a keyboard, which joints should stay fairly straight, not bent sharply up or down?
quests.hint: They are the narrow joints just below your hands.
quests.explanation: Keeping your wrists straight and relaxed helps your hands move comfortably.
quests.funFact: Short breaks to shake out your hands help them feel fresh.

quests.instruction: When you feel nervous, you may notice which part of your body creeping up toward your ears?
quests.hint: Your arms hang from them.
quests.explanation: When you are tense, shoulder muscles tighten and lift. Letting them drop can help you feel calmer.
quests.funFact: A slow, deep breath and dropped shoulders can help you relax.

quests.instruction: Before a soccer game, you jog and swing your legs gently. This warms up which parts so they are ready to work?
quests.hint: They get tight if you start out fast without warming up.
quests.explanation: Warm muscles stretch more easily and move better, so a gentle warm-up helps you play well.
quests.funFact: Muscles make up roughly a third of your body's weight.

quests.instruction: Jumping and running put gentle pressure on which parts, helping them grow strong?
quests.hint: They are hard, and exercise makes them denser.
quests.explanation: Bones respond to use. Jumping, running, and playing help them become stronger and denser.
quests.funFact: The best time to build strong bones is during childhood and the teen years.

quests.instruction: Before running, you draw slow circles in the air with your foot. Which joint are you warming up?
quests.hint: It sits just above your heel.
quests.explanation: Ankle circles warm up the joint and the muscles around it, which helps you stay steady on uneven ground.
quests.funFact: Ankle twists are common in sports like basketball, so warming up is a smart habit.

quests.instruction: Bright screens right before bed can make it harder for which part to get sleepy?
quests.hint: It controls when you feel awake or sleepy.
quests.explanation: Bright light tells your brain it is daytime, which can make falling asleep harder.
quests.funFact: A calm routine, such as reading a book, helps your body get ready for sleep.

quests.instruction: A very big meal right before bed can make which part of your body feel uncomfortable while you try to sleep?
quests.hint: It is the part that works to digest your dinner.
quests.explanation: Your tummy is busy digesting after a large meal, which can feel uncomfortable when you lie down.
quests.funFact: Eating dinner a couple of hours before bed gives your body time to start digesting.

quests.instruction: While you sleep, which parts keep breathing for you without you having to think about it?
quests.hint: They swell and shrink with every breath.
quests.explanation: Your brain controls breathing automatically, so your lungs keep working all night.
quests.funFact: Sleeping children breathe more slowly than when they are awake.

quests.instruction: When you trim toenails, you cut them straight across so the corners do not dig into the skin of which parts?
quests.hint: You clip the nails after a bath, when they are soft.
quests.explanation: Cutting straight across keeps the corners from growing into the skin, which can hurt.
quests.funFact: Toenails grow about one millimeter a month.

quests.instruction: Which two bony bends of your body often get dry and rough, so a little lotion helps?
quests.hint: They are the hinge in the middle of each arm.
quests.explanation: The skin on elbows is thick and has few oil glands, so it can get dry. Lotion keeps it soft.
quests.funFact: Moisturizer works best when you put it on slightly damp skin.

quests.instruction: When you pull weeds in the garden, you wear gloves to protect which parts from thorns and dirt?
quests.hint: Gloves are made to fit them.
quests.explanation: Gloves shield your hands from scratches, thorns, and germs in the soil. Wash your hands afterward, too.
quests.funFact: Some plants, such as stinging nettles, sting the skin on contact.

quests.instruction: Carrots contain vitamin A, which helps keep which parts of your body healthy?
quests.hint: You are using them to read this.
quests.explanation: Vitamin A helps the eyes work well, especially in dim light.
quests.funFact: During World War II, a story said carrots gave pilots night vision, but the real secret was radar.

quests.instruction: Fruits, vegetables, and whole grains contain fiber, which helps food move smoothly through which part of your body?
quests.hint: It is the part that digests your food.
quests.explanation: Fiber is the part of plants that your body cannot fully digest, and it helps food move along.
quests.funFact: Fiber also helps you feel full.

quests.instruction: Fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and fish are good choices to keep which muscle in your chest healthy?
quests.hint: It pumps blood around your body.
quests.explanation: Healthy foods help your heart and blood vessels work well.
quests.funFact: Healthy habits that start in childhood can last a lifetime.

quests.instruction: When you take a bath, which parts of your head need washing behind them, where sweat and dirt collect?
quests.hint: You can wiggle a finger behind them.
quests.explanation: The skin behind the ears gets sweaty and oily, so a soapy cloth helps keep it clean.
quests.funFact: The skin behind the ears has oil glands, which is why it can get greasy.

quests.instruction: Near a stove or a spinning machine, which part should be tied back, if it is long, so it cannot get caught or burned?
quests.hint: You can braid it.
quests.explanation: Loose long hair can dangle into flames or machine parts, so it is safest to tie it back.
quests.funFact: Hair burns easily, so keep it away from candles and open flames.

quests.instruction: A grown-up shows you how to slice a soft banana with a safe knife. You curl which parts back like a claw to keep them out of the way?
quests.hint: They are the part of your hand closest to the blade, so they tuck in.
quests.explanation: Curling your fingers into a claw keeps your fingertips behind your knuckles, away from the blade.
quests.funFact: Many cooks learn the claw grip first, before they learn to chop quickly.

quests.instruction: A doctor presses a stethoscope against your upper body to listen to your heartbeat and breathing. Which part is it?
quests.hint: Your ribs are right there.
quests.explanation: The chest holds the heart and lungs, so a stethoscope placed there picks up their sounds.
quests.funFact: The stethoscope was invented in 1816 by a French doctor who rolled up paper to listen to a patient.

quests.instruction: A doctor taps just below your kneecap with a small rubber hammer, and your leg kicks up. Which joint did the doctor test?
quests.hint: It has a round bone at the front.
quests.explanation: The tap triggers a quick reflex, a small automatic kick that does not need a decision from you.
quests.funFact: Doctors use this test to check that the nerves and muscles in the leg are working.

quests.instruction: At a check-up, the doctor asks you to open wide and say "ahh" so they can look at which part at the back of your mouth?
quests.hint: Air and food both pass through here.
quests.explanation: Saying "ahh" lowers your tongue and opens the back of your mouth, so the doctor can see your throat.
quests.funFact: Doctors use a small light and a flat stick to see the throat clearly.

quests.instruction: Wearing sunglasses and not rubbing with dirty hands both look after the same part of you. Which one?
quests.hint: You use it to read this question.
quests.explanation: Sunglasses block glare and harmful sun rays, and clean hands keep germs away from your eyes.
quests.funFact: Good sunglasses should say they block UV, the part of sunlight that can harm eyes.

quests.instruction: I am covered in a hard coating called enamel. Brushing twice a day and eating fewer sticky sweets keep me strong. What am I?
quests.hint: Dentists check on me twice a year.
quests.explanation: Brushing removes germs, and fewer sweets means less sugar for those germs to turn into acid.
quests.funFact: A dentist can spot tiny problems early, before they start to hurt.

quests.instruction: A good night's sleep and a bike helmet both look after the same part. Which one?
quests.hint: It thinks, remembers, and decides.
quests.explanation: Sleep helps your brain rest and sort memories, and a helmet cushions it if you fall.
quests.funFact: Your brain is about 75 percent water, so drinking enough water helps it work well.

quests.instruction: You come in from the playground with a scraped knee and a hungry tummy. Which parts should you wash first, before you eat or touch the scrape?
quests.hint: They touch everything you do.
quests.explanation: Dirty hands can spread germs to food and into a scrape, so they come first. Then clean the scrape gently with water.
quests.funFact: Clean hands are one of the best ways to stop germs from spreading.

quests.instruction: A mosquito bite itches a lot. Scratching hard can break which part and let germs in?
quests.hint: It protects your body like a wrapper.
quests.explanation: Skin keeps germs out. Scratching can break it, so a cool cloth or a gentle tap helps instead.
quests.funFact: The itch comes from your body's reaction to the spit a mosquito leaves behind.

quests.instruction: A good rule for headphones is to keep the volume low enough that you can still hear someone talking next to you. Which parts does this protect?
quests.hint: They are where headphones sit, in or over.
quests.explanation: Loud music, even through headphones, can wear out the delicate parts of the ear, so lower is safer.
quests.funFact: Tiny hair cells inside the ear do the hearing, and loud noise can damage them for good.
